action: Know the safe route to the nearest shelter or raised pucca house. Keep mobile phones charged for emergency calls and SMS, and make a family communication plan.
Keep ration card, Aadhaar, voter ID, cash and other valuables together in a waterproof bag, ready to carry.
Keep cattle and animals in a safe shed with clean drinking water. Harvest mature crops as soon as heavy rain is forecast and store them in a safe place.
Listen to radio, watch TV or read newspapers for weather updates. Stay calm, ignore rumours and do not spread them.
If a flash flood is possible, move to higher ground at once. Be careful near streams and drainage channels that can flood suddenly.
When officials tell you to evacuate, go at once to a safe shelter or higher ground. Raise furniture and appliances onto beds and tables, and turn off power and gas before leaving.
Do not touch electrical equipment if you are wet or standing in water, and do not walk or drive through flowing flood water.
Keep a heatwave kit ready: water, ORS, hat or umbrella, hand towel and a hand fan.
Avoid going out in the sun between 12 noon and 3 pm, and avoid heavy work in those hours.
Drink water often, even if you are not thirsty. Use ORS, lassi, lemon water or buttermilk, and avoid alcohol, tea, coffee and fizzy drinks.
Wear light-coloured, loose, porous cotton clothes and cover your head with a cloth, hat or umbrella.
Sunstroke first aid: lay the person in a cool, shaded place, wipe the body with a wet cloth and pour normal-temperature water over the head to bring the temperature down.
Sunstroke first aid: if the person is awake, give ORS or lemon sarbat to drink, then take them to the nearest health centre at once or call 108. Sunstroke can be fatal.
Never leave children or pets in a parked vehicle, even for a short time.
Identify safe places in every room: under a strong table or bed, or against an inside wall, away from glass and heavy furniture that can fall. Practise with your family.
Repair deep cracks in walls and ceilings, fix shelves and heavy objects firmly to the wall, and ask an engineer before building or extending a house.
Drop to the floor, take cover under a sturdy table and hold on until the shaking stops. Stay away from windows and glass.
Do not run outside during the shaking because of falling debris, and do not use lifts.
Move to an open area away from buildings, streetlights and electric wires, and stay there until the shaking stops.
If trapped: cover your mouth with cloth, do not light a match, do not kick up dust, and tap on a pipe or wall or use a whistle. Shout only as a last resort.
